# telli: the AI voice platform for B2C revenue teams

Jul 30 3 min read

Expand image

#### the conversation gap

For the last 20 years, the way consumers interact with businesses has not changed much. Most communication still happens through calls, emails, SMS, forms, or WhatsApp messages. Companies have adapted to these channels, but behind the scenes most still run on the same stack of CRMs, call centers, tickets, queues, dashboards, and manual operational work, creating friction for both teams and customers.

That world is starting to change. Consumers are beginning to use AI agents to compare offers, get support, change contracts, reschedule deliveries, book appointments, and resolve issues. Some will still use the channels they know. Others will expect their personal AI assistants to talk to companies for them. For B2C companies, this shift creates a massive operating challenge: communicating wherever customers choose to communicate, while still running scalable operations and growing the business.

# Humara raises €1.2M Seed to set the standard for modern waste plants globally

May 6, 2026

Humara, the Galicia-based software company rebuilding how waste and recycling plants are designed and operated, today announced the close of a €1.2 million Seed round led by Impact Shakers, with new investor Inclimo joining and full follow-on participation from existing backers Zubi Capital, Ship2B Ventures and the company's angel syndicate.

Founded in 2021 by Laura Rodríguez Álvarez, Martín Nogueira Salgueiro and Víctor González, Humara replaces the spreadsheets and disconnected CAD files that still underpin most waste-plant engineering with a physics-based SaaS platform. Its software simulates 82 distinct waste materials through real separation equipment, compressing design cycles from roughly four months to a matter of days. To date, more than 250 plants across Europe and Latin America have been designed on Humara, with customers including Veolia, FCC, PreZero, EGF, Ecoembes and Bianna reporting cost reductions above 70% and faster, more confident bidding on complex RFPs.

## Arzana raises $4.3M to automate factory paperwork 

 

Zoe Seiler | Sep 25, 2026 | 6:00 am | 

From left: Mason Vander Pol, Arzana’s salesperson, and co-founder and CEO William Alexander attend a trade show to learn from manufacturers and how their AI models can help automate clerical work. Submitted photo.

Growing up around manufacturing in Okoboji, William Alexander wondered if there were ways to make administrative tasks more efficient to give manufacturers more time to focus on their specialties. 

After graduating from Stanford University, Alexander teamed up with classmate Marshall Kools to develop Arzana, which builds custom artificial intelligence models around client workflows and data, automating tasks such as quoting, order entry and scheduling. 

Kools was also raised around manufacturing, with businesses in his family going back five generations. 

“It’s been something that I grew up around, loved, enjoyed and did in college,” Kools said. “William was one of my best friends in college. Since 2022, he and I have always wanted to start a company together.”
